The window POV from 01:41 instead shows a dark-green box-body straight truck with a conventional cab parked right outside the booth windows, and the man walks to it as his vehicle. The interior wide shots of the same booth window wall (00:59-01:26, 01:50-01:58) show parked cars and a gabled building, with no large truck right outside. findings.invariant_violated: interior seen through front windows must match the interior set
findings.description: From outside (00:00-00:09), the front glass shows white walls with a stainless kitchen hood/pass-through and orange counter directly behind it. There is no booth row and no OPEN neon. The interior wide shots show a long room with a full wall of windows lined with booths and an OPEN neon in a back-wall window, and the kitchen pass-through sits on the back wall away from the glazing. The interior also shows a neighboring gabled building and parked cars outside, while the exterior shows the building standing alone in an empty lot. The exterior and interior do not describe the same footprint or glazing.

The exterior establishes the customer entrance as the glass door in the front facade, and the reverse at 00:45 shows the customer glass/EXIT door at the front end of the dining room. Yet the arriving customer first appears behind the far end of the counter, beside the staff door next to the kitchen pass-through, in the employee work area. He then walks around the counter end into the aisle. His route comes through the staff/kitchen side rather than any customer entrance. An off-screen back door could explain it, so confidence is low.
